summary: A 1963 steel CL-100 cab on a block base in the Cibola National Forest, first staffed in 1922. Closed to visitors under a Forest Service order reported through October 31, 2026.

facts.design: CL-100 all-steel cab on a block base about ten feet high, erected 1963; replaced an earlier frame cab similar to the L-4 design

access.note: Forest Service road and area closure order covers the road from the forest boundary to the lookout and the campground. Reported to last until October 31, 2026, while summit observatory buildings are removed.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Cibola National Forest, Mountainair Ranger District)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1922 is the first lookout cabin on the peak; 1963 is the present CL-100 cab that replaced it. The record's 1963 date fits the present structure.
Early 1922 newspaper clips reproduced by westlookouts say Capillo Peak; the NHLR and Forest Service use Capilla.

notes_for_editor: Current access: the Forest Service page and KRQE (posted July 10, 2026) both report a closure to October 31, 2026. Do not publish visit advice until it lifts. Staffing today is not known from any source read. The 1922-1940 dates and quotes were checked against the westlookouts transcriptions on 2026-10-08; the original newspapers were not checked. The NHLR gives a concrete block base and westlookouts a cinder block base, so the wording is kept generic. Climbability is not stated in any source. A 2006 forest closure notice on westlookouts concerns a different fire and was not used. The record's kind two_story and elevation 9,368 ft were not contradicted.
